cards.text: The Israelites and Moses, Israel's leader, are still on the move through the wilderness, camping place after place until they cross the Arnon, the border between the Moabites and the Amorites. Numbers even quotes a line about the Arnon from the Book of the Wars of the LORD. Friend, I sat in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS without moving an inch, and these folks pack up camp before I can blink.

cards.question: Next stop is a place called Beer, where the LORD speaks to Moses. Who does the LORD tell Moses to gather there?
At Beer, the LORD tells Moses to gather the people so He can give them ___.
True or false: at the well, Israel sings a song.

cards.text: The song starts, "Spring up, O well, all of you sing to it!" Then it says the well was hollowed out with scepters and staffs, and friend, I have NEVER seen anybody grab a scepter to dig a hole.

cards.question: A scepter isn't exactly a farmer's tool. In Israel's song at the well, who dug it?

cards.text: From the wilderness they keep going, stop after stop, until they reach a valley in Moab where the top of Pisgah overlooks the wasteland. If you're keeping a list, friend, put the pencil down and just know they're still moving.
Then Israel sends messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites. No sneaking around here, friend: they knock on the front door first.

cards.question: What do Israel's messengers ask Sihon for?

answers.text: Permission to pass through his land
A share of the water in his wells
Soldiers to help them fight Moab

cards.question: True or false: Israel promises Sihon they'll stay on the King's Highway the whole way through.
No fields, no vineyards, not even a drink from a well. How does Sihon answer Israel's request?

answers.text: He gathers his whole army and attacks
He lets them pass for a fee
He sends them on a longer road

cards.text: Sihon fights Israel at Jahaz, and Israel puts him to the sword. Israel takes his land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok.

cards.question: Israel's new land stops at the border of the Ammonites. Why does the text say it stops there?

cards.text: Israel captures all the cities of the Amorites and occupies them, Heshbon and all its villages included.

cards.question: Heshbon was Sihon's city. Before Israel came, Sihon had fought the former king of ___ and taken all his land as far as the Arnon.

cards.text: That's why the poets say, "Come to Heshbon, let it be rebuilt; let the city of Sihon be restored." Friend, when the angel called me out of that junk drawer, nobody wrote ME a poem, but Sihon's city gets a whole one.
The poem says a fire went out from Heshbon, a blaze from the city of Sihon, and it consumed Ar of Moab. Then comes the cry: "Woe to you, O Moab!"

cards.question: The poets' song calls Moab the people of Chemosh, a false god, and says daughters were given into captivity. Whose captives do they become?

cards.text: Then the poem turns: "But we have overthrown them; Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon."
So Israel settles into the land of the Amorites, and Moses sends spies to a place called Jazer. Friend, they JUST moved in and they're already checking out the next neighborhood.

cards.question: True or false: after the spies go to Jazer, Israel drives out the Amorites who were there.

cards.text: With Jazer's villages captured, Israel turns up the road to Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, comes out with his whole army to meet them in battle at Edrei. Friend, it's like finishing one giant project at work and your boss walks in holding ANOTHER one.

cards.question: Og and his whole army are out there at Edrei. What's the first thing the LORD tells Moses about Og?
The LORD says He has delivered Og into Moses' hand, along with all his people and his ___.
True or false: after the battle at Edrei, Israel leaves Og's land behind and moves on.

cards.text: So Israel strikes down Og, along with his sons and his whole army, until no remnant is left. And they take possession of his land.
